Google Releases agents-cli to Enhance Coding Assistants for Cloud Agent Development

03 Nov 2026, 12:36 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Editorial Desk · Source: github.com

2 min read

Key takeawaysA new toolset called agents-cli has been introduced to equip coding assistants with specialized skills and commands for building, evaluating, and deploying AI agents on Google Cloud. According to the published documentation, the utility is designed to work alongside existing coding assistants rather than replace them.

In this article

A new toolset called `agents-cli` has been introduced to equip coding assistants with specialized skills and commands for building, evaluating, and deploying AI agents on Google Cloud. According to the published documentation, the utility is designed to work alongside existing coding assistants rather than replace them.

What is agents-cli?

The repository describes `agents-cli` as a command-line interface and collection of skills aimed at transforming coding assistants into experts on the Gemini platform and Google Cloud agent stack. It reportedly integrates with assistants such as Claude Code, Codex, and the Antigravity CLI.

  • Primary Function: Provides CLI commands and skills for managing the agent development lifecycle.
  • Framework Support: Built to support ADK (Agent Development Kit) agents end-to-end.
  • Standalone Use: Can be operated directly from the terminal without a coding agent, though skills are intended to simplify AI-assisted workflows.

Key Technical Details and Requirements

Developers looking to utilize the tool must meet specific software prerequisites:

  • Python: Version 3.11 or higher
  • Package Manager: `uv`
  • Runtime Environment: Node.js

For local development tasks such as creation, execution, and evaluation, a local AI Studio API key can be utilized with Gemini and ADK without requiring an active Google Cloud account. However, cloud features and deployment require a Google Cloud project.

Telemetry and Privacy

By default, `agents-cli` records a single usage signal per command invocation to help improve the software.

  • Local Logging: Structured log entries (recording command names, exit codes, error classes, duration, and environment metadata) are written to the user's designated Google Cloud project via Cloud Logging.
  • Analytics Headers: Request headers transmit metadata like client versions, OS details, and architecture for analytics.
  • Opt-Out: Users can disable telemetry using environment variables and verify their status via the `agents-cli info` command.

How to Verify and Learn More

Interested users can review the official GitHub repository (`google/agents-cli`) to inspect release notes, installation instructions, and tutorials. Contributions, bug reports, and feedback can be submitted directly through the GitHub issue tracker or via email to the project maintainers.
